# Galaxy Bridge native QUIC dependency notices

Direct dependencies: quiche 0.29.3, boring 4.22.0, libc 0.2.177. Cargo.lock records exact registry SHA-256 checksums except for the explicitly vendored quiche source described below. Archives come from https://static.crates.io/crates/NAME/NAME-VERSION.crate. Verified toolchain URLs and checksums are recorded separately in Task 6e4 evidence. No SDK/toolchain executables are distributed.

Galaxy Bridge vendors quiche 0.29.3 at `native/galaxybridge-quic/vendor/quiche`.
Original crate SHA-256: `61166d27591eb7cb1310eec2b8fc6ae0e0686e9e4ed742a3ffc6317171175e7d`.
The sole local upstream-source change preserves BBR2's existing lower congestion
window bound when applying a pacing cap (`src/recovery/gcongestion/bbr2.rs`,
`limit_cwnd`: `max_cwnd.max(self.cwnd_limits.lo)`). This prevents an empty
connection from being unable to fit a single datagram on a very low-RTT path.
No upstream copyright/license text was modified; the original COPYING is
retained and reproduced below. This is a locally patched build, not a claim
that upstream released this correction. The native build-input hash includes
the vendored Rust sources and manifest.

The inventory includes build-only and platform-specific packages; Windows-only packages are not linked into either G0 artifact. SPDX expressions are upstream declarations. The Android probe statically links NDK r29 libc++/libc++abi and dynamically uses system Bionic.

## BoringSSL bundled by boring-sys 4.22.0

BoringSSL is a fork of OpenSSL. As such, large parts of it fall under OpenSSL
licensing. Files that are completely new have a Google copyright and an ISC
license. This license is reproduced at the bottom of this file.

Contributors to BoringSSL are required to follow the CLA rules for Chromium:
https://cla.developers.google.com/clas

Files in third_party/ have their own licenses, as described therein. The MIT
license, for third_party/fiat, which, unlike other third_party directories, is
compiled into non-test libraries, is included below.

The OpenSSL toolkit stays under a dual license, i.e. both the conditions of the
OpenSSL License and the original SSLeay license apply to the toolkit. See below
for the actual license texts. Actually both licenses are BSD-style Open Source
licenses. In case of any license issues related to OpenSSL please contact
openssl-core@openssl.org.

some authors is recorded for use of their work. (This is purely for our own
